# Log-epsilon selection and compactness of the unscaled contact parameter

This note isolates a possible further use of the quantitative face argument.
Section 1 is conditional on a uniform two-sided linear joint-value gap, which
is being proved separately. Section 2 spells out the additional actual joint
separator premise. Sections 3--4 are elementary consequences of the displayed
row identities and bounds. No OC conclusion is claimed.

## 1. Selecting a scale without differentiating an optimized value

Suppose an attained joint value b(epsilon) has, for 0<epsilon<=epsilon_bar,

    b_*+c epsilon <= b(epsilon) <= b_*+C epsilon,
    0<c<=C<infinity.

Assume lower semicontinuity sufficient for attainment on compact positive
epsilon intervals. For tau>0 minimize

    b(epsilon)-tau log epsilon

over this interval. The value tends to infinity as epsilon tends to zero.
For all small tau, the test epsilon=tau/C has value at most

    b_*+tau[1+log C-log tau].

The endpoint epsilon_bar has a fixed positive gap above b_* as tau tends to
zero, so no minimizer lies there. If epsilon_tau=tau s_tau, the lower bound
at the minimizing point gives

    c s_tau-log s_tau <=1+log C.

The left side tends to infinity at both zero and infinity. There are therefore
fixed positive constants a,b such that

    a tau <= epsilon_tau <= b tau.

This is an interior attained scale selection. It invokes no derivative of
b, no exchange of derivatives with minimization, and no rate of convergence
of the minimizing bodies.

## 2. The scalar equation in an actual joint separator

At an actual body/parameter/epsilon minimizer of

    beta_epsilon(C,L)-tau log epsilon,

suppose the audited nonregular joint covering construction applies with one
separator for body, parameter, and both signs of dot(log epsilon). Every
proper contact's buffer derivative in this scalar direction is its buffer
itself; atomic rows have zero buffer derivative. The common physical response
therefore has scalar coefficient Delta/M. The objective term contributes
-tau to every row and the separator weights sum to one. Both signs of the
scalar variation force exactly

    Delta=tau M.

This assertion requires the actual extended response construction; Section 1
alone does not produce a separator. Under it, bounded positive M and Section 1
give uniform positive lower and upper bounds for Delta/epsilon. The original
upper bound Delta<=epsilon S_max remains consistent with this equation.

## 3. A uniform upper bound for L from the actual rows

Here is a separate abstract lemma. Let M be bounded above and every positive
fiber have volume at least v>0. Suppose actual contact rows satisfy

    sum_i sigma_i bar_rho_i=dm/M,
    d bar_rho_i=(L/L_i)d rho_i,
    L/L_i<=A on rho_i-almost every point,
    integral log L dm=0,
    -sum_i sigma_i log L_i=K_V>=0.

Assume also the same-force relation

    sigma_i=kappa_i epsilon (L_i E_i/M)^(1/N)/Delta,
    sum_i kappa_i=K<=K_*,  E_i<=M,
    Delta/epsilon>=a_*>0.

The constant A is supplied, under the fixed-base and source-inball hypotheses,
by positivity of a source touching plane on its entire minimal base face.
This bound is separate from an assumed original-volume barycenter: the
original rows need not have their source means.

For 0<l<=1, l^(1/N)(-log l)<=N/e. Hence

    sum_i sigma_i(-log L_i)_+
       <=(1/a_*) sum_i kappa_i L_i^(1/N)(-log L_i)_+
       <=K_* N/(e a_*)=:B_*.

Since sum sigma log L_i<=0, its positive part is at most B_* as well. Thus

    sum_{L_i>T} sigma_i <=B_*/log T,  T>1.

The bounded row likelihood gives a target tail inequality:

    m{L>A T}/M <=sum_{L_i>T} sigma_i <=B_*/log T.       (1)

If L_max is achieved at x_0 in a fiber K_z, nonnegative concavity implies
L>=L_max/2 on (x_0+K_z)/2, which has volume at least 2^(-d)v.
If L_max>2A, set T<L_max/(2A) in (1) and let T increase to that value.
It follows that

    log[L_max/(2A)] <=2^d M B_*/v.

In particular

    L_max<=2A exp(2^d M_max B_*/v)=:L_*.

No bound on the number of source contacts appears in this proof. Only the
actual row mixture and the same-force relation are used.

## 4. Uniform source lower bounds and comparable weights

Assume every source has an own inball of radius r and all fibers lie in
B(0,R). Put theta=r/(r+2R). Concavity along a segment extended from any
point of the own fiber through y_i to the opposite point of its inball gives

    L_i>=theta max_{K_pi} L.

Consequently, using logarithmic normalization and L<=L_*,

    0=integral log L
      <=V_pi log(L_i/theta)+(M-V_pi)log L_*.

Thus

    L_i>=theta L_*^(-(M-V_pi)/V_pi)
       >=theta L_*^(-M_max/v)>0.

The source energies are also uniformly positive by the source inballs and
at most M. Therefore f_i=(L_i E_i/M)^(1/N) has uniform positive lower and
upper bounds. Since sigma_i=kappa_i f_i/(Delta/epsilon), the physical
kappa weights and original-volume sigma weights are uniformly comparable.

The same argument gives positive lower bounds for L on every fixed inner
core of each fiber. It does not alone give positive lower bounds at boundary
points or identify the limiting original-volume row barycenters. A complete
limit of the contact rows still needs to track measures and contact planes.

## 5. Dependencies that must remain explicit

The two-sided linear gap, joint attainment for the scalar-penalized problem,
and applicability of one joint nonregular separator are separate obligations.
The scalar penalty is useful precisely because it can give a lower bound on
Delta/epsilon without assuming differentiability of b. Until those obligations
are discharged, Sections 1--4 are a conditional mechanism, not a completed
new compactness theorem for all bad minima and not an OC proof.
